h1: The 8 Best Camera-Free Robot Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Camera-Free Robot Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 camera-free robot vacuums for privacy, scored on LiDAR, bump navigation and docks, from eufy to Roomba and roborock.
summary: The eufy Omni C20 is the best camera-free robot: vacuum and mop, a self-cleaning dock and no lens pointed at your floor. For raw power, the eufy C28 reaches 15,000 Pa. If you want LiDAR mapping on a budget, the Roomba 105 Vac does it. The cheapest route in is the slim eufy 11S MAX with plain bump sensors.
intro: Most flagship robot vacuums now carry a front camera for object recognition. It lets them dodge cables and socks, and it also means a lens is travelling around your bedroom and living room. Plenty of buyers would rather skip that trade.

Every robot here navigates without an onboard camera, using LiDAR, bump sensors or cliff sensors instead. We reviewed eight of them and ranked them on how well their camera-free navigation suits real homes, plus suction, mopping and dock convenience. Scores follow the Primea framework.

products.name: eufy Omni C20 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo
products.verdict: Vacuum, mop and self-cleaning dock with no onboard camera. The most complete private option.
products.description:
The Omni C20 combines vacuuming and mopping and navigates with structural and cliff sensors, so no lens captures images of your floor as it maps a room. The self-cleaning dock handles upkeep, and separate hardwood and carpet behavior suits mixed homes.

It ranks first because it is the only camera-free pick here that also washes its own mop. The eufy C28 beats it on suction and the Roombas on LiDAR, but none packages the whole job as completely.

Pick it if you want a private, hands-off machine for hardwood and carpet.
products.skipIf: You want the lowest possible price.

products.name: eufy C28 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo
products.verdict: 15,000 Pa and a spinning HydroJet roller mop. The camera-free scrubber.
products.description:
The C28 pairs 15,000 Pa suction with a HydroJet roller mop that scrubs the floor instead of trailing a pad, and no lens or object-recognition system is involved in its navigation. It also has a self-empty base.

That suction figure is the strongest in the lineup, which matters on rugs and in homes that track in dirt. It sits behind the Omni C20 mainly because the C20's self-cleaning dock handles more upkeep.

Best for homes with heavy dirt and rugs where scrubbing power matters more than anything.
cons: Less dock automation than the C20
products.idealFor: Rugs and heavy dirt, with privacy in mind.

products.name: roborock Q7 M5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop
products.verdict: LiDAR mapping, 10,000Pa and a dock rated up to 7 to 9 weeks. Camera-free and low maintenance.
products.description:
The Q7 M5+ maps with LiDAR instead of a camera and adds a dock that can run up to 7 to 9 weeks before the bag needs changing, a long gap for this class. It vacuums and mops at 10,000Pa.

It is a step below the eufy Omni C20 in features, because there is no self-washing mop, but it wins on how rarely you touch the dock. LiDAR works from laser distance rather than images, which suits the privacy goal.

Choose it if you want mapped cleaning and the longest gaps between maintenance.
products.idealFor: Mapped, low-maintenance cleaning with no camera.
products.skipIf: You want the mop washed automatically.

products.name: roborock Q10 S5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop
products.verdict: The same camera-free LiDAR as the Q7 at 10,000Pa. Strong on medium-pile carpet.
products.description:
The Q10 S5+ shares the Q7's camera-free LiDAR navigation and 10,000Pa rating, which makes it a strong choice for medium-pile carpet and shedding pets. It also vacuums and mops.

It costs slightly less than the Q7 M5+, and the differences between them are small, so which to buy depends on dock details. It lacks the longer stated dock interval of the Q7.

A fit for carpeted homes with pets that still want mapped, camera-free cleaning.
cons: Close to the Q7 in features
products.idealFor: Carpeted pet homes wanting no camera.
products.skipIf: You want the longest dock interval.

products.name: iRobot Roomba Max 705 Robot Vacuum with AutoEmpty Dock
products.verdict: LiDAR plus obstacle and anti-fall sensors and dual rubber brushes, all without a camera.
products.description:
The Roomba Max 705 uses LiDAR with obstacle and anti-fall detection sensors, none of which need a camera. Dual rubber anti-tangle brushes are built for carpet and hard floors, and the AutoEmpty dock keeps upkeep low.

It ranks fifth because it is vacuum-focused and the roborock and eufy picks above add mopping. For a house where hair and tangles are the main enemy, the rubber brushes are the real draw.

Good for homes with long hair and a mix of carpet and hard floor.

products.name: Shark Navigator Robot Vacuum with Self-Empty Base RV2120AE
products.verdict: Bump and cliff sensors, a self-emptying dock and a brush that resists tangles.
products.description:
The Navigator RV2120AE steers by bump and cliff sensors, with neither lens nor LiDAR turret. Pet hair is the target: the base empties itself and the brush roll resists tangling.

Because navigation is basic it does not plan neat rows or build detailed maps, which is why it ranks below the LiDAR models. In exchange you get a docked pet-hair vacuum at a gentler cost.

Best for pet owners who want a docked vacuum and accept simple navigation.
products.idealFor: Pet owners wanting a simple docked vacuum.

products.name: iRobot Roomba 105 Vac Robot Vacuum with LiDAR Navigation
products.verdict: LiDAR mapping and neat-row cleaning on a modest budget. No camera.
products.description:
The Roomba 105 builds its map with LiDAR, not a lens, and sweeps in defined rows instead of a random bounce. LiDAR measures distance with a laser, a different method from vision-based navigation.

It ranks seventh because it has no dock and no mop at this price, so the budget goes into navigation. If your floors need only vacuuming and you want orderly coverage, that is a good use of money.

A fit for small to mid-sized homes that value neat rows over extras.
products.skipIf: You need a dock or mopping.

products.name: eufy 11S MAX Robot Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: Slim, quiet and sensor-only. The cheapest guaranteed camera-free option.
products.description:
The 11S MAX is a vacuum-only model with a slim body that fits under low furniture, steering by bump and cliff sensors alone, with no lens or LiDAR turret. It runs quietly.

It ranks last for its feature list, but nothing here is simpler or more private, since it has neither a camera nor mapping. That is also why it makes sense for people who want zero data.

Best for small homes with low furniture and a strong preference for simplicity.
products.idealFor: Small homes wanting the simplest private robot.

whatMatters.detail: LiDAR spins a laser to measure distance and builds a map without capturing images. Bump and cliff sensors detect contact and edges. Both avoid a camera lens. Check the listing for the words LiDAR, bump or no camera before assuming a robot is camera-free.

Camera-based robots can recognize cables and pet waste, while camera-free ones may bump or drive over them. Pick up cables and socks before running. If your floor is cluttered, a LiDAR model with obstacle sensors copes better than bump-only.
LiDAR plans neat rows and remembers rooms, bump sensors bounce randomly and need more time. For a home over 1,000 sq ft, LiDAR saves battery. In a small room the difference is minor.

A robot without a camera can still send map data to the maker's cloud. If privacy is your real concern, read the app permissions and look for local control. Check the listing for app features and what the account requires.
Rubber brushes tangle less with long hair than bristles. Camera-free robots cannot avoid hair clumps, so a good brush matters. Look for anti-tangle or rubber brush roll in the specs.

faq.q: Do camera-free robot vacuums navigate worse?
faq.a: They can't recognize objects like cables or socks, so they may bump into them. LiDAR models like the Roomba Max 705 still map well and use obstacle sensors to compensate.
No. LiDAR uses a laser to measure distance and builds a map from those readings, not images. Roborock and Roomba LiDAR models here have no camera lens.

faq.q: Is the eufy Omni C20 worth the premium?
faq.a: If you want a hands-off mop, yes, since its dock washes the pads. If you only vacuum, the Roomba 105 Vac or roborock Q10 S5+ save money.

faq.q: Will a bump-sensor robot damage furniture?
faq.a: Bumpers are soft and light, so damage is rare. The eufy 11S MAX is slim and lightweight. It will tap furniture legs as it goes.

faq.q: Do I still need the app?
faq.a: For scheduling and maps, yes. Basic models like the eufy 11S MAX also run from a remote or button, so you can use them without sharing data.

faq.q: How do I prepare my floors?
faq.a: Pick up cables, socks and pet bowls before each run. Without a camera, the robot will not avoid them. Use no-go zones in the app for tricky areas.

finalTake: For most people the eufy Omni C20 is the right buy: it vacuums, mops, washes its own pads and has no onboard camera. For scrubbing power, the eufy C28 hits 15,000 Pa. For long gaps between maintenance, the roborock Q7 M5+ is rated up to 7 to 9 weeks. And for the cheapest private option, the eufy 11S MAX has bump sensors only.
